units.description: The value of one Roman numeral letter, given as its byte value c: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000 (upper case only). Any other byte, including lower case letters, digits, spaces and signs, gives 0.

pub fn test_value_2() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_value(86) == 5); return 0; }

units.description: Read the text s as a Roman numeral by the usual rule: sum the letter values from left to right, except that a letter whose value is smaller than the value of the letter after it is subtracted instead of added. Accept any letters I, V, X, L, C, D, M in any arrangement and do not judge whether the numeral is canonical (IIII reads as 4). If s is empty, or contains any byte that is not one of the seven upper case letters (a space, a lower case letter, a digit), answer -1. Never panics. Use roman_value for each letter.
tests: pub fn test_read_1() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("XIV") == 14); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_2() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("MCMXCIV") == 1994); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_3() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("IIII") == 4); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_4() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("MMMCMXCIX") == 3999); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_5() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("") == -1); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_6() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("xiv") == -1); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_7() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read(" X") == -1); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_8() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("XIV ") == -1); return 0; }
pub fn test_read_9() -> [] int { test.assert(roman_read("X2") == -1); return 0; }

units.signature: fn to_roman[&h](heap: &!h Heap, n: int) -> [heap] result.Result[buffer.Buffer, &static [byte]]
units.description: The Roman numeral for n as owned text (a buffer you return), or Err with a short message if n is outside 1..3999 (so 0, negative numbers and 4000 or more are Err). The numeral is the canonical shortest form: write each decimal digit of n on its own, thousands first, using I, V, X, L, C, D, M; the subtractive pairs are IV (4), IX (9), XL (40), XC (90), CD (400) and CM (900); never write more than three equal letters in a row. Examples: 1 is I, 4 is IV, 14 is XIV, 40 is XL, 1994 is MCMXCIV, 3999 is MMMCMXCIX. Upper case only.
tests: fn cases_to_roman_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }

fn cases_to_roman_ok[&h, &w](heap: &!h Heap, a1: int, want: &w [byte]) -> [heap] int { match to_roman(heap, a1) { result.Result::Ok(v) => { var same = false; borrow v as &x in { same = cases_to_roman_same(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, v); if same { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn cases_to_roman_err[&h](heap: &!h Heap, a1: int) -> [heap] int { match to_roman(heap, a1) { result.Result::Ok(v) => { buffer.drop(heap, v); return 2; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_to_roman_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_to_roman_ok(heap, 1, "I"), 0); return 0; }

units.description: The integer the text s stands for, as Ok(n), or Err with a short message if s is not a valid numeral. Accept ONLY canonical numerals: compute n with roman_read; if that is -1 or n is outside 1..3999, it is Err. Otherwise build to_roman(n) and it is Ok(n) only if its bytes are exactly the bytes of s; any other text (IIII, VV, VX, IC, IL, XM, VIV, IXI, CMC, CDC, MMMM, lower case, the empty string, spaces, digits) is Err. Never panics on any text. Free the built text before returning. Compare bytes with a loop, not with buffer equality.
tests: fn cases_from_roman_ok[&h, &t1](heap: &!h Heap, a1: &t1 [byte], want: int) -> [heap] int { match from_roman(heap, a1) { result.Result::Ok(v) => { if v == want { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn cases_from_roman_err[&h, &t1](heap: &!h Heap, a1: &t1 [byte]) -> [heap] int { match from_roman(heap, a1) { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 2; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_from_roman_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_from_roman_ok(heap, "MCMXCIV", 1994), 0); return 0; }
